objective: Theory spec of the B/C ratio in the 1D thin-disc diffusion model of theory:cr-secondary-ratio (equivalent weighted slab), with its degenerate direction D0/L

model.description: 1D diffusion halo of half-height L with a thin gas and source disc of half-thickness h, D(R) = D0 beta (R/R0)^delta, no convection, reacceleration, energy losses or decay; equivalent to a weighted slab with lambda_esc = n_H m_H h v L / D

assumptions: steady state; free escape at |z| = L; observer at the mid-plane z = 0
thin disc (h << L): gas and sources in 2 h delta(z); hydrogen target only
kinetic energy per nucleon conserved in fragmentation (straight-ahead)
parents (C, O) are pure primaries with observed ratios given as input; one effective stable secondary
cross sections are inputs: effective cumulative, energy independent, ILLUSTRATIVE values
local interstellar ratio: no solar modulation

conventions.unit_system: CGS for transport (cm, s, g; D in cm^2/s, n_H in cm^-3, grammage in g/cm^2); lengths L and h given in kpc (1 pc = 648000/pi au); kinetic energy per nucleon in GeV/n; rigidity in GV; cross sections in mb (1 mb = 1e-27 cm^2) [crsr:C05]
conventions.scales: reference rigidity R0 in D(R) = D0 beta (R/R0)^delta (benchmark R0 = 1 GV); weighted slab: lambda_esc(R) = lambda0 (R/R0)^-delta
conventions.energy_variable: kinetic energy per nucleon E/n in GeV/n, conserved in fragmentation (straight-ahead); the ratio compares fluxes at the same E/n
conventions.frame: Galactic rest frame (interstellar gas at rest); observer at the disc mid-plane z = 0
conventions.mass_approximation: nucleus mass = A x atomic mass unit (0.93149410242 GeV; binding energy neglected), so all species share beta at fixed E/n; rigidity R = (A/|Z|) p_per_nucleon via core/kinematics/relativistic.py; target hydrogen mass m_H = proton mass 1.67262192369e-24 g (electron and binding neglected) [crsr:C05]
conventions.crsr:observable: B/C = N_B / N_C, interstellar fluxes of an effective single boron species (A = 11, Z = 5) and carbon (A = 12, Z = 6) at the same E/n, at z = 0, before solar modulation
conventions.crsr:cross_sections: input sets under models/ (xs-*.json): effective cumulative production sigma(j -> B) and inelastic sigma_i on hydrogen, energy independent; the shipped sets are ILLUSTRATIVE placeholders; a choice between sets is a model-alternative uncertainty object
conventions.crsr:bin_average: a binned value is the ratio averaged uniformly in ln(E/n) over the bin (Gauss-Legendre, 8 nodes), not the ratio of bin-averaged fluxes
conventions.crsr:transport_model: diffusion-1d: thin disc of half-thickness h and density n_H in a halo |z| < L with N(+-L) = 0, D(R) = D0 beta (R/R0)^delta, no convection, reacceleration, losses or decay; weighted-slab: exponential path-length distribution with mean lambda_esc

extension.order: not-applicable (classical transport model, no perturbative expansion)

scales.meaning: reference rigidity of the diffusion coefficient

validity_domain.geometry: h << L (thin disc); corrections O(h/L) quantified in the benchmark
validity_domain.physics: energies where convection, reacceleration and energy losses are negligible; the model is not claimed to describe low energies

checks_run.name: slab path-length average equals the closed form (SymPy)
thin-disc jump solution and linear halo profile (SymPy)
thin disc equals weighted slab with lambda_esc = n_H m_H h v L / D (SymPy)
ratio invariant under D0 and L scaled together, not under D0 alone (SymPy and numerical)
finite-disc closed form solves both regions and matches at z = h (SymPy)
slab ODE integration averaged over the path-length distribution vs closed form
finite-volume solution vs finite-disc closed form
finite-disc ratio tends to the thin-disc closed form as h/L -> 0
units and dimensions (grammage in g/cm^2, ratio dimensionless)

checks_not_run: comparison with a published numerical B/C benchmark (open question B1)
comparison with any propagation code (none run)
neglected: energy dependence of the cross sections
